question.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{4}),$ where $x$ is measured in degrees?. Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.worked_solution:
The asymptotes of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ are given by the expression

$$
x={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘},
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{4}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{x}{4}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{x}{4}={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{4} & ={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & ={360}^{∘}+n\cdot {720}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x={360}^{∘}+n\cdot {720}^{∘},$ where $n$ is an integer.
